52376.text: Consider the following vision defects listed in Columns I and II and the corrective measures in Column III. Choose the correct combination. Column   I Column   II Column   III P. Hypermetropia ( i ) Near-sightedness a. Convex lens Q. Myopia ( i ) Far-sightedness b. Concave lens
52376.sol: Hypermetropia is far-sightedness, a vision condition in which nearby objects are blurry. It is corrected by using convex lens or positive power lens. Myopia is near-sightedness, a condition in which close objects appear clearly but far ones do not. It is corrected using concave lens or negative power lens. In hypermetropia, image is formed behind the retina, while in myopia image is formed in front of the retina.

refractive index of adhesive glue is close to that of glass
adhesive tape is more transparent than glass
52429.sol: Frosted glass has a rough layer which causes irregular refraction and makes glass translucent. When a transparent tape which has refractive index close to that of glass is pasted over the rough surface of glass, the tape glue fills the roughness of glass. 79932.sol: Secondary succession occur where vegetation was present previously, but vegetation was destroyed due to natural or artificial causes i.e. fire, flood, sudden changes in climate landslide. 84076.subject: Zoology
84076.text: The hepatic portal vein drains blood to the liver from
84076.sol: The hepatic portal system is found in all vertebrates. The flow of deoxygenated blood from the digestive and absorptive parts of the alimentary canal (especially from the intestine) to the liver before returning to the systemic circulation is called hepatic portal circulation. The blood which comes from the alimentary canal contains absorbed food such as glucose, amino acids. The excess of glucose is converted into glycogen and is stored in the liver for later use.

The interphase lasts more than 95% of the duration of cell cycle. 123656.subject: Botany

To increase the chromosome number by half

This specialised kind of cell division that reduces the chromosome number by half results in the production of haploid daughter cells. This kind of division is called meiosis. The colour of dorsal side of body is generally olive green with dark irregular spots. On the ventral side the skin is uniformly pale yellow. The frog never drinks water but absorb it through the skin. Body of a frog is divisible into head and trunk A neck and tail are absent. Above the mouth, a pair of nostrils is present. 127966.text: How is urea transported to the kidneys in frogs?
127966.sol: The elimination of nitrogenous wastes is carried out by a well developed excretory system. The excretory system consists of a pair of kidneys, ureters, cloaca and urinary bladder. These are compact, dark red and bean like structures situated a little posteriorly in the body cavity on both sides of vertebral column. Each kidney is composed of several structural and functional units called uriniferous tubules or nephrons. Two ureters emerge from the kidneys in the male frogs. The ureters act as urinogenital duct whic

128002.sol: Frogs have well organised male and female reproductive systems. Male reproductive organs consist of a pair of yellowish ovoid testes , which are found adhered to the upper part of kidneys by a double fold of peritoneum called mesorchium. Vasa efferentia are 10-12 in number that arise from testes. They enter the kidneys on their side and open into Bidder’s canal. Statement (B) is correct according to NCERT; the primary oocyte completes its first meiotic division within the tertiary follicle, which then matures into the Graafian follicle. 128596.sol: Epinephrine is an adrenal medullary hormone that causes fight-or-flight responses like piloerection and pupillary dilation. Cortisol is a glucocorticoid from the adrenal cortex that produces anti-inflammatory reactions and suppresses the immune response. Aldosterone is a mineralocorticoid that acts mainly at the renal tubules and stimulates the reabsorption of Na ^+ and water. 129356.subject: Zoology
129356.text: The nerve centres which control the body temperature and the urge for eating are contained in
129356.sol: Hypothalamus is the part of the sides and floor of the brain derived from the forebrain. It lies at the base of thalamus. The hypothalamus contains a number of centres, which control body temperature, urge for eating and drinking. It also contains several groups of neurosecretory cells, which secrete hormones called, hypothalamic hormones.

129370.sol: Nerve cells are unable to divide because they lack centrioles, which plays important role in cell division. Centrioles help to arrange the microtubules that move chromosomes during cell division to ensure each daughter cell receives the appropriate number of chromosomes. While all other cells in our body have capacity to regenerate/self-repair. Related Theory Our brain is evolved to process complex tasks at a higher pace than other living beings. The brain achieves this with help of the whole nervous system, which

129662.sol: CO₂ is removed from our body by lungs.

130908.subject: Zoology
130908.text: How often does menstruation occur in human females on average?
130908.sol: The reproductive cycle in the female primates (e.g. monkeys, apes and human beings) is called menstrual cycle. The first menstruation begins at puberty and is called menarche. In human females, menstruation is repeated at an average interval of about 28/29 days , and the cycle of events starting from one menstruation till the next one is called the menstrual cycle.

131189.sol: The correct sequence of events in Human Reproduction is Gametogenesis → Insemination → Fertilisation →Implantation → Gestation → Parturition

131404.subject: Zoology
131404.text: What is the linkage formed between the nitrogenous base and OH of 1'C pentose sugar?
131404.sol: A nucleotide has three components – a nitrogenous base, a pentose sugar (ribose in case of RNA, and deoxyribose for DNA), and a phosphate group. There are two types of nitrogenous bases – Purines (Adenine and Guanine), and Pyrimidines (Cytosine, Uracil and Thymine). Cytosine is common for both DNA and RNA and Thymine is present in DNA. Uracil is present in RNA at the place of Thymine. A nitrogenous base is linked to the OH of 1' C pentose sugar through a N-glycosidic linkage to form a nucleoside , such as adenosine

131536.subject: Zoology
131536.text: Who developed the chemical method to synthesize RNA molecules with defined combinations of bases?
131536.sol: Providing proof that the codon was a triplet, was a more daunting task. The chemical method developed by Har Gobind Khorana was instrumental in synthesizing RNA molecules with defined combinations of bases (homopolymers and copolymers). Marshall Nirenberg’s cell-free system for protein synthesis finally helped the code to be deciphered. Severo Ochoa enzyme (polynucleotide phosphorylase) was also helpful in polymerising RNA with defined sequences in a template independent manner (enzymatic synthesis of RNA).

131542.subject: Zoology
131542.text: What is degeneracy in the genetic code?
options: The ability of the code to read in a contiguous fashion
The presence of punctuation in the code
The ability of a single codon to code for more than one amino acid
The universality of the code across different organisms
131542.sol: The salient features of the genetic code are as follows: (i) The codon is triplet. 61 codons code for amino acids and 3 codons do not code for any amino acids, hence they function as stop codons. (ii) Some amino acids are coded by more than one codon, hence the code is degenerate. (iii) The codon is read in mRNA in a contiguous fashion. There are no punctuations. 133747.subject: Zoology
133747.text: What is the purpose of primary treatment of sewage?
133747.sol: Primary treatment basically involves physical removal of particles – large and small – from the sewage through filtration and sedimentation. These are removed in stages; initially, floating debris is removed by sequential filtration. Then the grit (soil and small pebbles) are removed by sedimentation.

The sticky ends are formed precisely because the enzyme cuts the DNA helix a little away from the centre of the palindromic recognition sequence, but between the same two bases on the opposite strands. 134839.text: Match List I with List II. List I List II A. Exonuclease I. Removes nucleotides from the ends of the DNA B. Endonuclease II. Makes cuts at specific positions within the DNA C. EcoRI III. Cuts the DNA between bases G and A producing sticky ends D. Palindromic sequence IV. Sequence of base pairs that reads same on the two strands when orientation of reading is kept the same Choose the correct answer from the options gi
134839.sol: According to NCERT, exonucleases remove nucleotides from the ends of the DNA, whereas endonucleases make cuts at specific positions within the DNA. EcoRI is a restriction endonuclease that recognises the palindromic sequence GAATTC and cuts the DNA between bases G and A, producing sticky ends. A palindromic sequence in DNA is a sequence of base pairs that reads the same on the two strands when orientation of reading is kept the same. Therefore, the correct matching is A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV. Answer: A-I, B-II, C-II

135481.subject: Zoology

135481.sol: Homeothermic are the animals having a nearly uniform or constant body temperature. These animals are known as warm blooded animals, eg, birds, man. Poikilothermic are those, having a variable temperature which fluctuates with that of environment. They are called the cold blooded animals, eg, reptiles, amphibians.

6a13e469688ac6d0667aad66.subject: Biology
6a13e469688ac6d0667aad66.text: In the methodology of the Human Genome Project, the blind approach of sequencing the whole set of genome that contained all the coding and non-coding sequences, and later assigning functions to different regions is referred to as
6a13e469688ac6d0667aad66.sol: The Human Genome Project used two major approaches for sequencing the genome. The first approach focused on identifying all the genes that are expressed as RNA, which is referred to as Expressed Sequence Tags (ESTs). The second approach was a blind approach of simply sequencing the whole set of genome that contained all the coding and non-coding sequences, and later assigning different regions in the sequence with functions. This approach is referred to as Sequence Annotation. Answer: Sequence Annotation

X^c X^c : Colour blind daughter 3. X^C Y : Normal

95214.sol: Lateral meristem is the meristem which occurs on the sides and is helpful in increasing width of stem and root. 95267.subject: Botany
95267.text: Cells of ________ tissue are living, show angular wall thickenings and provide mechanical support.
95267.sol: Collenchyma, part of the ground tissue, is a simple living tissue found in plants. Collenchyma layer is generally found below epidermis of the plant. They are either found in a patch manner or even distributed throughout. The cell wall of collenchyma tissue cells is thickened at corner due to higher deposition of cellulose, pectin and hemicellulose. The cells are generally spherical or polygonal in shape. 95313.subject: Botany
95313.text: Bidirectional translocation of solutes takes place in:
95313.sol: Sugars produced in sources, such as leaves, need to be delivered to growing parts of the plant via the phloem in a process called translocation, or movement of sugar. The points of sugar delivery, such as roots, young shoots, and developing seeds, are called sinks. It is done by phloem tissue.

96385.subject: Botany

96385.sol: Dead plant remains such as leaves flower, bark and dead remains of animals including fecal matter constitute detritus which is the raw material for decomposition. Earthworm breakdown detritus into smaller fragments to increase surface area for further enzymatic activity.

96746.subject: Botany
96746.text: Which of the following statements about the nitrogen cycle are false? 1 . Rhizobium and Frankia cause nitrogen fixation in their independent free-living stage. 2 . Nitrobacter oxidizes nitrites to nitrates.
96746.sol: Free living nitrogen fixing aerobic microbes are Azobacter and Beijerinckia while Rhodospirillum is anaerobic and free living. Cyanobacteria such as Nostoc are also free living nitrogen fixers. Rhizobium has a symbiotic relationship with roots of legumes like, pea, lentils, alfalfa etc. They produce nodules on the roots. Similar to this is Frankia which also produces nitrogen fixing nodules on the roots of non-leguminous plant Alnus. Ammonia is first oxidised to nitrite by the bacteria Nitrosomonas and/or Nitrococc

96896.sol: Allium cepa is onion. It shows cymose inflorescence with umbellate clusters. It consists of a number of short flower stalks which spread from a common point like umbrella. During unfavourable conditions, it forms a fleshy structure called bulb for storage of food in their scale leaves. It is placed in family Liliaceae in which colchicine Colchicum autumnale is also placed. In its flowers, the petals and sepals cant be differentiated. This whorl is called perianth and it is made of tepals.

97118.sol: Depending on the arrangement from where they develop, the fruit can be categorized as simple fruits, aggregate fruits, multiple fruits, and accessory fruits. When a fruit develops from a single ovary (monocarpellary) of a single flower it is known as a simple fruit, eg: plum and peaches, which may be fleshy, and walnuts which fall in the dry category. 97213.text: In humans, the activation of sympathetic nervous system stimulates the adrenal medulla to release certain hormones that help in flight and fight response. A similar type of response in plants can be given by
97213.sol: Abscisic acid (ABA) is an inhibitory plant hormone also known as 'dormin' hormone as it promotes seed dormancy and inhibits growth. ABA is a stress hormone as it helps the plant survive different kinds of environmental stresses. It also stimulates the closure of stomata. It acts as the antagonist of the gibberellic acid.

97316.subject: Botany
97316.sol: Gibberellic acid (GA 3 ) was one of the first gibberellins to be discovered and remains the most intensively studied form. All GAs are acidic. They produce a wide range of physiological responses in the plants. Their ability to cause an increase in length of axis is used to increase the length of grapes stalks. Gibberellins, cause fruits like apple to elongate and improve its shape. They also delay senescence. Thus, the fruits can be left on the tree longer so as to extend the market period. 97864.subject: Botany
97864.text: Which one of the taxonomic aids can give a comprehensive account of complete compiled information of any one genus or family at a particular time?
97864.sol: Taxonomic keys are aids for the rapid identification of unknown plants. Flora is an inventory of the plants of a defined geographical region. A herbarium is a safe place for storing specimens as well as provide a suitable atmosphere for research. A monograph is a comprehensive taxonomic treatment of a taxonomic group, generally a genus or a family, providing all taxonomic data relating to that group.
